segments.title: Chương 298: 0300【Dư Luận Đảo Chiều】
segments.content:
Some online opinion leaders, after getting paid, would post a single article and then ignore the matter completely.

Some, however, were just despicable.

Despite being paid for only one article, he would proactively provide follow-up services. Perhaps unable to find any other explosive topics, he would pop up from time to time to mock Chen Guiliang.

Because insulting Chen Guiliang and *Future Epoch* brought in traffic!

After most of the online trolls had quieted down, Chen Guiliang suddenly posted several articles on his personal Hainei Net account.

Posting these things when the public outcry was at its peak would have been useless, because the haters would have just claimed they were fabricated.

The first article wasn't a game development log, but the "*Hope* (tentative game title) Project Proposal."

The date marked on the project proposal was June 18, 2005.

The second article posted was a technical exchange agreement between Game Science and Pixel Soft.

The agreement was signed on July 20, 2005, and its content was a request for Pixel Soft to impart skills on fighting game engine development.

Only the third article was a game development log, dated August 15, 2005. The project leads wouldn't even be in place for several more months, and the game's name hadn't been officially decided, but they had already begun fumbling their way through engine development.

The fourth article was a rewritten game project proposal, dated September 17, 2005, titled "*Future Epoch (NeoFutureAscent)* Project Proposal."

At this point, the game's name was officially confirmed, and Shuxia Yehu was brought on as the game's story planner.

Chen Guiliang also emphasized, "The first project proposal predates the launch of *DNF*, and the proposal's content had already established it as a side-scrolling fighting MMORPG."

"Furthermore, the technical exchange agreement with Pixel Soft also predates the launch of *DNF*. This collaboration was for the purpose of self-developing a fighting engine. If anyone has doubts, you can seek confirmation from CEO Liu of Pixel Soft."

The boss of Pixel Soft, Liu Kun, also had a registered account on Hainei Net.

When asked by netizens, Liu Kun answered very clearly: "Back then, Chen Guiliang said he wanted to make a side-scrolling fighting MMORPG, which is why I lent him two engine developers. Everyone knows these two; they were the engine developers for *Blade & Sword*."

Then Liu Kun added: "Our technical staff were deeply involved in the initial development of the 'Future' engine and could create a similar engine at any time. If the time is right, Pixel Soft will also produce a side-scrolling fighting MMORPG."

Subsequently, the two engine developers from Pixel Soft also came forward to confirm that they had spent three months on exchange at Game Science. They also stated that they and the other developers had never heard of *DNF* at the time.

Netizens, who had already calmed down, didn't even bother to read the project proposals and development logs in detail before they believed this reversal and became supporters of Chen Guiliang.

Many netizens who had been cursing Chen Guiliang just half a month ago were now helping him curse the haters.

Quite a few people also flocked to the official website of *Future Epoch*, because more development logs were posted there, albeit with many key details redacted.

These people just wanted to know why the development of *Future Epoch* was so slow.

And then, they repeatedly saw one name: Feng Ji!

The project lead mentioned Feng Ji repeatedly in the development logs, and his tone was quite helpless. Because of the reasonable suggestions Feng Ji made, many details had to be redone. There was even one dungeon that was completely scrapped and remade from scratch.

"CEO Chen, who is Feng Ji?" fans came to ask Chen Guiliang.

Chen Guiliang replied on his personal account: "Feng Ji is a newcomer. After graduating with a bachelor's degree, he hung out in internet cafes for over a year playing *World of Warcraft*. He was introduced to Game Science by a friend early last year and started by doing odd jobs on the project team... Currently, Feng Ji has been confirmed as the project lead for *My Own Swordsman*. Here is a link to his Hainei Net account."

The netizens grew even more curious.

"Hanging out in internet cafes for over a year after graduation? Got introduced to Game Science to do odd jobs? Became the project lead for *My Own Swordsman*? I don't get this resume at all."

"This guy must be Chen Guiliang's relative, right?"

"In the development logs for *Future Epoch*, the project lead was almost driven crazy by Feng Ji."

Indeed, many people had been driven crazy by Feng Ji.

Because at the time, Feng Ji's own experience and abilities were insufficient, yet he insisted on pursuing perfection and reason. So he would always raise problems, but couldn't provide solutions or improvements himself.

Everyone would proceed with the original plan, and Feng Ji would continue to participate. As they worked, Feng Ji would suddenly come up with a good idea. Everyone would discuss it in a meeting and realize it was indeed a feasible approach.

And so, they would scrap everything and start over.

Once would have been fine, but this happened many times with Feng Ji. Sometimes his suggestions were ignored, but most of the time they were adopted.

Feng Ji carried a laptop with him, but most of the time it wasn't connected to the internet, used purely for taking work notes.

Only after receiving a call from Chen Guiliang did Feng Ji go online to reply to the netizens.

"Hello everyone, I'm Feng Ji. I am currently in charge of developing *My Own Swordsman*, and I am on a research trip at Yanmen Pass. We have already visited the ancient cities of Datong and Pingyao. Next, we will be visiting large and small cities in Jin Province and across the country. During our urban research, we will also collect local music, paintings, sculptures, customs, languages, and so on..."

"I'm a newcomer to the gaming industry and don't know anything, so I can only do my best. For the last three months of last year, and the first two months of this year, I was constantly auditing history classes at Tsinghua and Peking University. I searched for historical documents in the libraries of Qing-Bei..."

"I hope that when players enter *My Own Swordsman*, it will be like they've traveled back to the real Ming Dynasty!"

After reading Feng Ji's reply, the netizens were all stunned.

To develop a game, he actually went to Tsinghua and Peking University to audit history classes for half a year? And he still had to conduct research on ancient cities, folk music, paintings, sculptures, and customs all over the country...

A netizen from Jin Province said: "Those photos Feng Ji posted are indeed of Datong Ancient City, Pingyao Ancient City, and Yanmen Pass."

Another netizen said: "With this kind of attitude towards making games, how many can you find in the whole world? I'm so moved I'm about to fucking cry."

Another netizen commented: "No wonder there's been no news about the game *My Own Swordsman*. Turns out for the better part of the last half-year, the project lead was auditing history classes at Qing-Bei, and now he's off doing field research... He's insane! Never mind how much money it'll cost, the time commitment alone will be huge. Who knows when in the hell this game will ever be finished."

A netizen predicted: "I think I'm seeing the rise of China's Blizzard."

Chen Guiliang seized the opportunity and launched the official website for *My Own Swordsman*.

There was no other content on the website, only set after set of photographs.

For example, the photos of him auditing history classes at Qing-Bei were "work photos" that Feng Ji had taken himself. He had to document everything in case others in the company questioned whether he was just taking money to have fun.

These work photos now became promotional photos for the game.

Beneath each photo, there was a text description.

"October 9, 2006, attended my first class at Peking University. A little excited. The lecturer is a famous professor..."

"October 12, 2006, attended my first class at Tsinghua University..."

The last few sets of photos were all from the field research, and now featured a team of three.

Feng Ji had become visibly scruffier. He was too lazy to even shave his stubble, and he would often wear the same jacket for a week or two.

People who work earnestly will always be recognized.

And they can inspire deep appreciation.

After appreciation comes protectiveness.

Damn it, Game Science is putting so much heart into making games, and you haters still come to cause trouble!

Many well-known bloggers, including Wuyue Sanren, were swarmed.

Wuyue Sanren stared at his computer screen, sweating.

He wasn't afraid of being swarmed, because the more he was swarmed, the more buzz he generated.
